svg.aria-label: STM32MP257F-DK boot chain: the Boot ROM loads TF-A BL2 from the fsbla1 partition into on-chip SYSRAM; BL2 trains the LPDDR4 memory and loads BL31, OP-TEE and U-Boot from the FIP; BL31 stays resident as the EL3 secure monitor; OP-TEE runs at S-EL1 and serves SCMI clock and reset requests; U-Boot runs at non-secure EL1, reads extlinux.conf and starts the Linux kernel.
svg.text: How the STM32MP257F-DK boots, and what this repository builds for each stage
Power-on to login prompt: each stage loads the next. BL31 and OP-TEE stay resident after Linux is up.
copies BL2 from partition fsbla1 into SYSRAM and jumps to it (BL2 is built with RESET_TO_BL2: it runs at EL3 straight after the ROM).
BL2 opens the FIP (found by partition TYPE GUID 19d5df83-…, or the name 'fip'), loads BL31 into SYSRAM, OP-TEE into DDR, U-Boot and its DTB into DDR.
BL31 runs OP-TEE once so it can initialise (and serve SCMI), gets control back, then ERETs to U-Boot at non-secure EL1 (STM32MP_BL33_EL1=1).
STILL IN MEMORY WHILE LINUX RUNS
Boot ROM, BL2: finished (SYSRAM is reused)
BL31 stays at EL3 for good: every SMC goes through it; PSCI (CPU on/off, suspend, reset) is served from SYSRAM
OP-TEE stays at S-EL1, reached through BL31: SCMI server (clocks, resets) and trusted applications
Addresses: BL2/BL31 from plat/st/stm32mp2/stm32mp2_def.h and the linker map of this build; OP-TEE and U-Boot from fdts/stm32mp257f-dk-ca35tdcid-fw-config.dtsi,
STM32MP_BL33_BASE and u-boot include/configs/stm32mp25_common.h (kernel_addr_r). Red = secure world, blue = boot stages, teal = Linux, slate = hardware.
